logs: Review of hook-runner-b: Not ready to build on: 6 major and 6 minor findings. The checks pass and the wiring is right, and refresh and release work in the main cases. But there are four problems. (1) The StoreBusy seam reads busy.entries, while records sets busy.released, so entries released under a busy flush are never logged as lock.released and release() returns []. The test mocks a StoreBusy shape records never raises. (2) The tmp class is wrong. On macOS it never matches, because gettempdir() is not resolved, so temporary paths are classed 'outside'. Where the temporary directory is not a symlink, it overlaps the project's own classes, and two test_classes tests then fail on Linux; I reproduced that with a resolved TMPDIR. (3) A broken classes.toml gives rule_error, not the promised policy_invalid, on product paths. (4) Classes are matched on the resolved path only. The design says both the literal and the resolved path, and classes_of resolves its input, so no rule can get the literal path's classes. On the outcomes: P3BLD-14 is confirmed by mutation. P3SEAM-24 and the refresh half of P3OPS-20 are in the code, but test_lock_refresh cannot fail without them: every case uses the holder's own session id, and dropping run and story kept all 7 liveness tests green. P3OPS-20 is also marked fixed while its clear half stays with B8.. 12 findings, 6 blocker or major.
Round 1 for hook-runner-b: 15 of 17 fixes confirmed, 3 still open.
Round 2 for hook-runner-b: 2 of 3 fixes confirmed, 2 still open.

Faults log runner.liveness_error and never block. hooks.json regenerated; wiring and ctx tests updated; 4+7 new tests including loud-failure and flush-lock-held cases; latency median under threshold. Closed P3BLD-14, P3SEAM-24, P3OPS-20 (refresh half; clear half to probe B8). Updated run-lock.md, rule-model.md, event-types.toml; spec_lint clean; outcomes recorded; findings.py build confirmed.

The StoreBusy seam of liveness.release follows the concurrent records fix round's contract as the task note stated (StoreBusy carrying the released entries) instead of the plan's silence on it; test_release_logs_a_busy_store pins the shape.

still_open.problem: Fixed for the probe the finding named: brief.md -> src/main.rs spelled via /var, or via a tmp_path alias, now gives ('brief','spec-product','source','project'), and a mutation confirms the new test catches it. Not fixed in general. The fallback anchors at os.path.realpath(literal.parent), which collapses every directory symlink, not only the root's spelling. A path through an in-project directory symlink, spelled through an alias of the root, anchors outside the root; _anchored then answers None and only the resolved form is classed. That is the finding's own failure. Portable probe with src/dirlink -> /etc: <project>/src/dirlink/hosts gives ('source','project','unclassified','outside'), but <alias>/factory-project/src/dirlink/hosts gives ('unclassified','outside'). On macOS the same happens with /var and /tmp spellings.
still_open.proposed_fix: Before the realpath(parent) fallback, walk literal.parents and anchor at the first ancestor whose realpath equals the resolved root: root.joinpath(literal.relative_to(ancestor)). Keep the current fallback after the walk. Prototyped in a scratch copy: both spellings then give ('source','project','unclassified','outside') and all 160 tests in tests/hooks pass. Add the alias-spelled src/dirlink/hosts case to test_classes.py.
